Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Generator scaffolding left in: oaicite, [cite: 1], placeholders -- finish the text and read it
- The "it's not X, it's Y" construction -- just state Y
- A bolded word opening a list item as a per-item tag -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- Saying "is" the long way: serves as, boasts, functions as -- use the plain verb
- One-line dramatic fragments: "That's it. That's the whole thing." -- cut them, the preceding sentence already made the point
- Em dashes clustering in one document -- most drafts need 0-2; use commas, periods or parentheses for the rest
- Filler verbs: leverages, facilitates, unlocks -- use a plain verb, or cut the sentence
- A snake_case identifier written as plain prose -- name it in words, or mark it as inline code
- Marketing cliches: "hidden gem", "let's dive in" -- say the specific thing
- The "Not X. Not Y." listing construction -- state the point once
- Stock section skeleton: "Despite its success", "Looking ahead" -- name the specific thing the section is for
- Standalone filler adverbs: undoubtedly, arguably, notably, importantly, ultimately -- most add nothing; cut them unless one is carrying real emphasis
- A banned synonym of one of this project's canonical terms, per its declared lexicon -- one word, one meaning: use the canonical term the word's own note names
- Dramatic turning points with nothing concrete behind them: "Everything changed." -- name the actual event, or cut it

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

# Pricing

Free for one developer. Paid when your team needs shared standards and a record of what was found.

## Solo ($0)

Review your own commits on one repository, public or private. You get the full check set, inline comments on every pull request, and 30 days of history. No card required. The cap is one seat and one repository; when you pass it, you can upgrade without moving anything.

## Team ($18 per developer, monthly)

Everything in Solo, across every repository you own.

Shared rule sets mean two reviewers hold the same line. Findings stay for a year, long enough to show whether the same class of bug keeps coming back. Merge protection holds a branch while a high-severity finding is open, and notifications go to Slack or email.

We bill per developer who actually pushed that month, so a contractor between projects costs nothing.

## Enterprise (talk to us)

For teams whose compliance requirements the other tiers can't satisfy. Runners live inside your VPC, so source never leaves your network. SAML sign-on, SCIM provisioning, and audit logs you can export to your SIEM. You get a named support engineer with a four-hour response commitment, plus custom checks written against your internal style guide and maintained by us as it changes.

## Details

Annual billing takes 15% off Team.

Cancel from the dashboard and billing stops at the end of the period; nothing renews silently. Public repositories with an OSI-approved license get Team features at no cost, no application required.

Change nothing else, and keep the same length and purpose.
